newsitem.title: USA: Chicago area water agency seeks fix for bond woes.
newsitem.headline: Chicago area water agency seeks fix for bond woes.

text.p: The Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago is seeking a legislative remedy that would allow it to continue to issue bonds for water and flooding projects, a district official said Monday.

Hugh McMillan, general superintendent of the agency, said a number of bills are pending before the Illinois General Assembly that would losen constraints on debt issuance imposed by state property tax cap and debt limitation laws.

The district, which serves Cook County, has about $1 billion of general obligation debt outstanding, but needs to sell nearly another $1 billion of debt for ongoing and future projects, McMillan said.
However, the district's hands are tied by the laws which limit property tax levy growth and require a voter referendum for new GO debt.

McMillan said that given the size of the county, voters in one part which does not experience flood problems, were not likely to approve debt for flooding projects in another part of the county. Still, the district is responsible for alleviating flooding problems throughout the county, he added.
And it is the district's charge to raise the necessary local funds to attract a match of federal funds for the projects, according to McMillan.
One bill would exclude debt service payments on bonds sold for flood-control projects from a current levy limit of $141 million in annual debt service, he explained.
The district has also found itself unable under the debt limitation law to refund outstanding debt, he added.

"We've been sitting on the fence waiting for the market to be positioned to do a refunding," he said, adding that the district cannot legally refund the $100 million of GO bonds because it would exceed the $141 million annual debt service levy limit.

Another bill would allow the district to issue new limited tax GO bonds for its massive Deep Tunnel project as outstanding debt is retired. While a 1995 law enabled municipalities in Cook County to sell new debt as old debt retired as long as they do not exceed their debt service levy limit, the water district was not granted those powers, McMillan said.

The district is also seeking to extend a statutory sunset scheduled for Dec. 31, 2001 on its ability to issue bonds. McMillan said that sunset was imposed in the 1970s when the district turned to debt issuance after funding projects on a pay-as-you-go basis. Now with federal feet-dragging on funding, he said the sunset needs to be extended.
Still another bill would extend the final maturity on district debt to 30 years instead of 20 years to help level out debt service payments, McMillan said.
He said the district was "fairly confident" the legislation would pass, as some bills have already moved out of committee.
